instructions: Read this roster before every scheduled reading run; work only inside the registered slot.

Never read a title listed in the agent's completed_books unless the user explicitly requests a reread. If the user does not specify a new title, continue the agent's last unfinished current_book first; after completion, select the most recently added unread book on the user's bookshelf, excluding completed_books. Do not default to selecting by author.

Before starting, read agent-communication.md (compact index) and today's Asia/Shanghai agent-communication/YYYY/MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md, then check the roster and latest registry for the assigned slot, a running task, and conflicts. Read older daily files only for relevant cross-day handoffs or evidence, not all history; do not start if the active state is unclear.

For any failure, interruption, access block, conflict, or uncertain result, notify the user immediately in the current Cue private conversation with what actually happened and the next recovery step. A repository update alone is not a notification.

At run start, set run_status to running and append the actual start time, current book, and slot to agent-communication/YYYY/MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md for the actual event date in Asia/Shanghai, never to the compact index. Create the daily file and its month navigation entry when absent, following agent-communication.md.

At run end, update run_status, actual end time, book_completion, and a minimal output reference in this roster, and append an end event to the appropriate dated communication file. Cross-midnight events use their own event dates with the same run ID and a start-date reference; clearly label backfilled records.

At each reading run start, send the user a brief direct Cue message naming the slot and book. After each run, send a direct Cue result with actual measured duration, real chapter/post/section titles and truthful content coverage (partial versus complete), and a concise mind-map summary based only on content actually read.

For future new reading, use verified chapter/post/section titles and headings as user-facing navigation, not page numbers/counts or page-turn counts. If a title is unconfirmed, say so and describe only verified content; never invent a locator. Leave old books, published notes and historical reading/page references unchanged. Report interrupted or unstarted runs and recovery steps promptly.

Every configured time slot is an independent reading run and must read even if another slot on the same date completed. Never overlap an active run; if another run's status is unclear, verify it is no longer active before starting, or report the unresolved conflict.
Same-book work from multiple slots on one date is merged into a single date note; different books read on the same date each get their own date note.
If an agent misses a slot, record that fact; do not overlap another agent's window or claim the missed run happened.
Use unknown/needs-confirmation rather than guessing a book, completion state, or execution result.
This public file records only minimal coordination metadata; never include passwords, tokens, private messages, or book-note content.
